key_insight: ETCH-X combines composable, heterogeneous datasets with a modular fitting pipeline to deliver both fine-grained (hands/face) expressiveness and global robustness to clothing, occlusion, and noisy/partial scans in parametric body fitting.
problem_solved: Makes parametric body fitting (e.g., SMPL) reliably work on clothed humans captured in the wild, closing the typical trade-off between local detail and robustness to clothing, pose variation, noise, and missing data.
method: Compose diverse datasets (real scans, synthetic clothed models, partial/noisy captures) into a unified training scheme so the model sees broad variations and generalizes across domains.

Modular two-stage pipeline: a robust global alignment stage for pose/shape under clothing and occlusion, followed by local expressive refinement modules specialized for hands, face, and fine geometry.
Training and losses tailored for clothing-aware fitting and robustness (occlusion-aware losses, composable augmentations, and domain-mixing priors) to reduce failure modes on in-the-wild scans.
impact: Provides AI/ML teams a practical way to obtain accurate, expressive parametric fits from noisy/clothed 3D captures, reducing manual cleanup and enabling higher-quality downstream tasks like animation, retargeting, and texturing.

paper_title: ETCH-X: Robustify Expressive Body Fitting to Clothed Humans with Composable Datasets
paper_authors: Xiaoben Li, Jingyi Wu, Zeyu Cai, Yu Siyuan, Boqian Li
